en.name: Macarons, French
en.summary: French macarons keep 1–2 days at room temperature and 3 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Refrigerate them if they are not eaten right away: the shells are meringue, but the ganache or buttercream between them is a perishable filling.
en.pantry: 1–2 days at room temperature in a closed box. The shells themselves are almond meringue — sugar, egg white and ground almond, baked dry — and would keep far longer on their own. What limits a macaron is the filling and the moisture moving out of it into the shells: a good macaron is one that has already softened slightly, and by the second day at room temperature it is going soggy. Do not leave them out in a warm humid kitchen, and if they are not going to be eaten right away, put them in the fridge.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for macarons, only the instruction to refrigerate them if they are not eaten right away. That instruction is about the filling, not the shell: a ganache, a buttercream or a fruit curd is a perishable food that belongs at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in a sealed box. Keep them away from anything strongly smelling — meringue and butter both pick up fridge odours quickly — and let them come back to room temperature before eating, because a cold macaron tastes of very little.
en.freezer: 3 months at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality, and macarons freeze unusually well: pastry shops do it routinely. Freeze them in a single layer in a rigid box so nothing crushes them, with paper between layers. Kept continuously frozen they stay safe beyond that window; the limit is drying, ice crystals and freezer burn. Filled shells freeze better than bare ones, which crack and go brittle.
en.thawing: Thaw them in the fridge, still in the closed box, then bring them to room temperature before opening it. Opening a cold box in a warm kitchen puts condensation straight onto the shells and makes them sticky.
spoilage: Shells gone soggy, collapsed or weeping sugar syrup.
A sour or off smell from a dairy filling.
Mould spots, most often on a fruit or cream filling rather than on the shell.
Shells cracked, dry and hollow after a long spell in the freezer.
tips: Box them rigid; macarons are broken far more often than they go bad.
Thaw in the closed box so condensation forms on the box, not on the shells.
Serve at room temperature — cold mutes almost all the flavour.
Keep them well away from strong-smelling food in the fridge.

faq.q: How long do French macarons last?
faq.a: 1–2 days at room temperature, or 3 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). Refrigerate them if they are not going to be eaten right away.
Yes, 3 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and they freeze unusually well. Box them rigid with paper between the layers and thaw in the closed box.

faq.q: Do macarons need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: If they are not eaten right away, yes. The shell is meringue, but the ganache or buttercream filling is perishable. No refrigerated duration is published for them.

zh.name: 法式馬卡龍
zh.summary: 法式馬卡龍放室溫可放 1～2 天，−18 °C 冷凍 3 個月。沒有要馬上吃就放冷藏：外殼是蛋白霜，但夾在中間的甘納許或奶油霜是會壞的餡。
zh.pantry: 裝在密閉盒子裡放室溫 1～2 天。外殼本身是杏仁蛋白霜——糖、蛋白和杏仁粉烤到乾——單獨放可以撐久得多。真正限制馬卡龍的是餡，以及水分從餡往外殼移動這件事：好吃的馬卡龍本來就已經微微回潤，而放到室溫第二天它就開始變得軟塌。又熱又濕的廚房裡不要把它擺在外面，若沒有要馬上吃，就放冷藏。
zh.fridge: 馬卡龍沒有公布的冷藏期限，只有「沒有要馬上吃就冷藏」這條指示。這條指示講的是餡而不是殼：甘納許、奶油霜或水果餡都是易腐食品，該放在 4 °C 以下、裝在密閉盒裡。要離味道重的東西遠一點——蛋白霜和奶油都很會吸冰箱的味道——而且吃之前先回到室溫，因為冰冷的馬卡龍幾乎嚐不出味道。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 3 個月品質最好，而且馬卡龍出乎意料地耐凍：甜點店本來就是這樣做的。單層平放在硬盒裡冷凍，層與層之間夾紙，才不會被壓壞。只要全程沒退冰，超過這個期限仍然安全；限制它的是變乾、冰晶和凍燒。夾好餡的比空殼更耐凍，空殼容易裂、容易變脆。
zh.thawing: 連盒子一起放冷藏解凍，回到室溫之後再開盒。在溫暖的廚房裡直接打開冰冷的盒子，水氣會直接凝在殼上，馬卡龍就變黏了。
spoilage: 外殼軟塌、塌陷，或滲出糖漿。
乳製餡料聞起來發酸或有異味。
長霉，通常先長在水果或鮮奶油餡上，而不是殼上。
在冷凍放太久，外殼裂開、變乾變空心。
tips: 用硬盒裝；馬卡龍被壓碎的機率遠高於壞掉。
連盒解凍，讓水氣凝在盒子上而不是殼上。
回到室溫再吃——冰冷會把香氣壓掉大半。
冰箱裡務必遠離味道重的食物。

faq.q: 法式馬卡龍可以放多久？
faq.a: 室溫 1～2 天，或 −18 °C 冷凍 3 個月。沒有要馬上吃就放冷藏。
可以，−18 °C 下 3 個月，而且非常耐凍。用硬盒、層間夾紙，解凍時連盒一起。
沒有要馬上吃就需要。外殼是蛋白霜，但甘納許或奶油霜餡是會壞的。它並沒有公布冷藏的可放天數。
